[id="model-cache-known-limitations_{context}"]
= Model cache known limitations

[role="_abstract"]
Model cache is a Developer Preview feature in {productname-long}.
Review the following limitations and constraints before using model cache in your environment.

:feature-name: Model cache
include::snippets/developer-preview.adoc[]

[id="model-cache-feature-limitations_{context}"]
== Feature limitations

The following limitations apply to model cache:

.Model cache feature limitations
[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Limitation
|Description

|No cross-namespace sharing for network volumes
|Models cached by using a custom `StorageClass` are namespace-scoped.
Only `InferenceService` or `LLMInferenceService` resources in the same namespace as the persistent volume claim can use the cached model.
To use the same model in many namespaces, create a separate `LocalModelCache` resource in each namespace.
Cross-namespace sharing is supported only for local disk caching.

|No automatic model eviction
|Model cache does not automatically remove cached models when storage space is low.
You must manually delete `LocalModelCache` resources to reclaim storage space.
Monitor the `storageLimit` and `used` fields in the `LocalModelNodeGroup` status to track storage consumption.

|Models are immutable
|You cannot update a cached model in place.
To cache a new version of a model, delete the existing `LocalModelCache` resource, and then create a new resource with the updated `sourceModelUri`.

|No built-in authentication or authorization for cached models
|Model cache does not provide access control for cached model files.
Any `InferenceService` with a matching `storageUri` can use a locally cached model.
Use namespace-level access control and RBAC policies to restrict access to inference services.
|===

[id="model-cache-security-constraints_{context}"]
== Security constraints

Model cache requires specific security configurations on {openshift-platform} clusters:

.Model cache security constraints
[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Constraint
|Description

|Custom security context constraints (SCCs)
|The model cache controller applies custom SCCs to download job pods and agent DaemonSet pods.
These SCCs grant the elevated permissions required for reading and writing model files on local node storage.

|Namespace pod security admission
|The download job namespace might require elevated pod security admission labels to allow the download jobs to run with the required security context.

|File system permissions
|The host directory for local model storage must have ownership set to `1000:1000` to match the default user in the download job container.
Wrong ownership causes download jobs to fail with permission denied errors.
|===

[id="model-cache-scheduling-constraints_{context}"]
== Scheduling constraints

Inference pods that use cached models are subject to the following scheduling behavior:

* *`CrashLoopBackOff` during download*: If an inference pod is scheduled to a node where the model download has not completed, the pod might enter a `CrashLoopBackOff` state.
The pod recovers automatically after the download finishes on that node.
Check the `nodeStatus` field in the `LocalModelCache` status to verify the download progress on each node.

* *Node affinity*: For local disk caching, inference pods are scheduled only to nodes where the model is cached.
If no node has completed the download, the pod remains in a `Pending` state.
